change.display_text: Two identical blocks start from rest at the same height. One falls vertically; the other slides down a straight frictionless slope inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where 0 < θ < 90°. Both reach the ground with the same speed. Which reaches the ground first?
change.excerpt_note: Adapted from the linked source to assess only this topic.

answer.text: The vertically falling block arrives first. Its acceleration is g; the sliding block has acceleration g sin θ and travels a longer distance. tslide = tfall/sin θ > tfall.
